answer: We model identity multiplication through a cryptographic prism, splitting resources to simulate independent actors. To enforce Sybil resistance, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds are distributed across a dense shale of multi-tiered validation pools. Here, each zero-knowledge verifiable delay function generates a distinct signal of true computation. Combined with a subgame-perfect slashing matrix that wipes out staking collateral, the expected utility of identity replication is strictly negative, forcing a robust Nash equilibrium.
